newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach down after negative press comment.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach down after negative press comment.

text.p: Shares in British transport group Stagecoach Plc dropped in pre-market trading on Monday, extending recent declines amid negative press comment on its market valuation.
The stock was down 39p at 640 by 0820 GMT in volume of 23,000 shares.

The Financial Times Lex column put a valuation of 540p on Stagecoach based on what it said were "far from gloomy" assumptions about its bus operations, its South West Trains unit and Porterbrook rolling stock leasing company.

Stagecoach shares dropped 52p on Wednesday and Thursday last week amid fears of tighter regulatory controls should the opposition Labour party, running ahead in opinion polls, win the election on May 1.
The company's South West Trains has been fined for missing performance targets and could even be stripped of the franchise if it continues to underperform.

The recent reversal in Stagecoach shares is in marked contrast with its spectacular gains of last year, when they more than doubled in value on the back of the company's successful expansion from buses into rail operations.
